recommendations.rationale: Transmission is the preferred geometry for clear, semi-transparent liquids such as whey, and NIR is the most common in-line method with fiber probes. A transflection probe can in some cases serve both low-fat and high-fat streams, which is exactly the variation here.
recommendations.conditions: Applies while the stream stays within the pathlength the probe can handle; if it becomes too opaque for the light to penetrate, a reflection geometry is needed.

citations.quote: Transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate.
In some cases, a Transflection probe can already be a combined solution working well for low-fat and high-fat containing milk products.
Near-IR vibrational spectroscopy (NIR) is the most common online analysis method performed using fiber optic probes.

recommendations.rationale: Diffuse reflection is used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, so it is the counterpart to test for the turbid operating state. Reflection is sensitive to surface characteristics and particle size, so scatter correction and its own calibration are needed.
recommendations.conditions: Applies mainly to the more turbid state; for clear liquid it is less representative than transmission.

citations.quote: NIR Reflection is primarily used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates.
reflection can work well in highly scattering environments but can be less representative for clear liquids.
the method is sensitive to the surface characteristics and fat globule size.

recommendations.rationale: MIR ATR gives well-defined fundamental bands with high selectivity and is not limited by pathlength, so it is the fallback if the NIR models do not resolve the protein signal in the turbid state. Combining NIR with MIR is a hypothesis to test against the best single method, not a demonstrated gain for this stream.
recommendations.conditions: Applies only if the single-method NIR tests do not reach the required protein accuracy and the MIR probe contact, fouling and fiber link prove workable.

solution_options.fusion_note: Level: one calibration per method first, then low-level fusion of the joined spectra with block scaling so neither block dominates the model. Both probes must look at the same small area of the flowing stream, their data must be aligned to a common time step, and each block needs its own calibration and diagnostics. The second instrument is only worth keeping if the fused model beats the best single NIR model on independent batches.

One of the challenges of multispectral analysis is the need to simultaneously connect at least two independently operating measuring instruments.

assessment.chemometrics_note: NIR bands overlap, so a chemometric calibration is required, and it is specific to the matrix: a model built on one whey composition must be re-validated when the stream or product changes. The laboratory protein values are the reference data for building and validating that model.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: The measurement point is in-line and continuous, and fiber probes allow on-site analysis with results in near real time, which suits a stream that changes during operation rather than grab sampling.
assessment.future_direction: Once the informative wavelengths are known, a compact LED-based optical multisensor system could be a later step for this measuring point.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the measured turbidity stays low in all operating states, the single-probe option O1 becomes sufficient; if NIR cannot reach the required protein accuracy, the combined option O3 becomes the candidate.
proposal.next_step: Run the feasibility experiment on clear and turbid whey samples with laboratory protein references, then review the results with AFS.

assessment.brief_answer: Test NIR first, using a transmission/transflection geometry for the clear state and a diffuse-reflection geometry for the more turbid state, with laboratory protein values as the reference. A single transflection probe may already cover both states, so it is the least-effort first test. A MIR-ATR add-on is only a later option if NIR cannot reach the required protein accuracy. The turbidity range, accuracy target and reference method are still open.
